summary: No Puducherry-specific trans-related law, enforcement series or incident pattern is documented. As a union territory with a partial legislature, state-level protective policy here depends on the Union government - RTI research into India's transgender welfare boards notes that union-territory structure among the drivers of the welfare-board gap.

sources.summary: Human Rights Watch dispatch (26 March 2026) on the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill passed by Parliament: it removes the right to self-identification affirmed by the 2014 Supreme Court ruling, limits legal recognition to historically recognised socio-cultural groups (hijra, kinnar) and intersex people, drops recognition for self-identified trans men, trans women and non-binary people, mandates medical certification for identity documents, and in HRW's assessment increases the risk of wrongful prosecution; protests followed the vote in Mumbai and elsewhere.

BBC report (26 March 2026): Parliament passed the amendment bill changing how transgender people are legally defined and recognised; the government says it makes welfare benefits more accessible and strengthens the 2019 law against exploitation and trafficking, while critics warn it would exclude many trans, non-binary and gender-fluid people from legal recognition; notes roughly two million transgender people in India and the bill awaiting presidential assent; cited as the current national framework shift bearing on every state and union territory.

Times of India (18 August 2024, Kolkata): a group of trans women travelling to a medical college reported that a railway protection force constable groped one of them at a metro station while 'checking her gender', with an FIR filed and intrusive questioning reported; cited in the country dossier as an example of the document-and-body 'gender check' harassment trans people face at transport hubs - a West Bengal incident with no direct bearing on Puducherry.

localsOnly: Welfare-board status and the documentation machinery of the 2019 Act and its 2026 amendment are resident-facing: the union-territory dependency described above bears on services and certificates for local transgender people rather than on how visitors are treated.
